description: We are AEVION, a team from Jazan building a digital dashboard that gives astronauts a clear picture of their health in one view. It compares wristband data with each astronaut's own baseline, shows a status with a reason and next step, and works without contact with Earth. Our team covers research, UI/UX, presentation and programming. We welcome members skilled in space or health science, data analysis, or wearables.
summary: AEVION is a digital health dashboard for astronauts on long missions to the Moon and Mars. In these missions, contact with Earth is delayed, medical help is limited, and health data is scattered across devices and reports. AEVION puts it all in one clear view. It reads wristband data, compares it with each astronaut's own baseline, and shows one status (green, yellow or red) with the reason and the next step. It also includes a daily exercise plan that adapts to sleep and readiness, periodic lab trends with a ready note for the doctor, and an emergency flow with saved steps that work without contact with Earth. When contact returns, data is sent automatically. We built an interactive prototype with simulated data, using NASA Human Research Program hazards and risks and NASA astronaut exercise data. AEVION helps astronauts act early and gives doctors organized data. It does not diagnose.
details:
What it does. AEVION is one dashboard with four parts:

  1. Readiness: reads wristband data (heart rate, sleep, activity, light) and compares it with the astronaut's own baseline. Example: sleep 1.3 hours below baseline gives 72/100, yellow, with advice to go lighter on cardio.
  2. Daily workout: keeps the medical exercise prescription and adapts the day to sleep and readiness. A virtual run, goals and challenges make it more engaging.
  3. Periodic labs: latest versus previous results, trend and status, an 8-week chart with the alert limit and personal baseline, and a ready note for the doctor.
  4. Emergency: choose yourself or a crewmate, then the type (heart, breathing, cabin, radiation, injury, crewmate not responding). Saved steps work offline, and data is sent when contact returns.

Benefits and impact. Earlier awareness of body changes, faster decisions without waiting for Earth, and organized data for doctors.

Creativity. A personal baseline instead of general values; a reason and an action with every alert; three alert levels to avoid alarm overload; offline operation; and a crewmate's vitals shown only in an emergency.

Factors we considered. Delayed contact, limited medical support, and NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight. AEVION does not diagnose. Lab ranges are experimental, and emergency steps are demo guidance, not an official medical protocol.

Tools and data. Interactive prototype with simulated data. NASA Human Research Program hazards and risks, NASA astronaut exercise data, and CSA radiation monitoring.

Code github : https://github.com/Aevion-prog/aevion.git
